en: Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-sub-periods (pratyantardaśā), Chapter 61.

One should multiply the duration of each individual planet by its own period-measure to obtain the inner period (antardaśā). One should then divide [the sum] by the total of all periods; thus, the results for each successive inner period are obtained in order. (1)
Dispute, loss of wealth, distress for one's wife, and pain in the head—these are to be known by the wise as the results occurring during its sub-period (pratyantara). || 2 ||
One should know that agitation, quarrels, loss of wealth, and mental anguish are the results occurring within the sub-period of the Sun during the major period of the Moon. || 3 ||
Fear of kings, fear of weapons, imprisonment, many perils,
and suffering caused by enemies and fire are the results during the sub-period of Mars.
During the sub-period of Rāhu, the results are: phlegmatic diseases, fear of weapons, loss of wealth, great terror, defeat by the king, and likewise anxiety. (5)
The destruction of enemies, victory, prosperity, the acquisition of garments, gold, and ornaments,
as well as the gain of horses, vehicles, and so forth— these are the results during the sub-period of Jupiter.
Loss of wealth, suffering for one's livestock, great agitation, and severe illnesses—
during the sub-period of Saturn, a person encounters all such inauspiciousness.

In the interval between the asterisms, there will be the acquisition of knowledge, union with kinsmen, the attainment of food, the arrival of wealth, the gain of merit, and honor from the king. || 8 ||
Fear for one's life, great loss, fear of the king, and conflict with enemies, as well as a great dispute, shall occur during the sub-period of Ketu. (9)
In this period, the days will be of uniform appearance, gains here will be meager,
and the attainment of happiness will be very slight during the sub-period of Śukra.

The attainment of land, food, and wealth, honor from the king, and great happiness—these gains are to be known as occurring within the period of the Moon; such is the fruit within the sub-period of the Moon. 11.
During the sub-period of Mars, there will be an increase in intelligence, great honor, happiness with kinsmen, the acquisition of wealth, and fear of enemies. (12)

O twice-born one, during the sub-period of Rāhu, there may be the attainment of auspicious things and the acquisition of royal wealth; however, due to inauspicious influences, there will also be minor illnesses and death.

The acquisition of clothing, great splendor, and the knowledge of Brahman from a true guru, as well as the attainment of a kingdom and ornaments—these are the fruits within the period of the Guru. 14.
On an unfavorable day, one suffers affliction, especially from wind and bile disorders;
during the sub-period of Saturn, there will be loss of wealth, grain, and reputation. (15)
During the sub-period of Mercury, there shall be the attainment of the great festival of a son's birth, the acquisition of knowledge, high advancement, and the gain of white garments and food. (16)
During the sub-period of Ketu, there occurs conflict with a Brāhmaṇa, untimely death, the destruction of happiness, and suffering arises in every respect. (17)
During the sub-period of Venus within the major period of the Moon, there is the acquisition of wealth, great happiness, the birth of a daughter, excellent food, and affection from all people. (18)
There is the arrival of food, the acquisition of clothing, the destruction of enemies, the onset of happiness, and the attainment of victory everywhere during the solar revolution of the Moon. (19)
During the sub-period (antardaśā) of Mars within the major period (daśā) of Mars, one should predict fear of enemies, terrible strife, hemorrhaging, and the fear of death.
During the sub-period of Rāhu, there shall be imprisonment, defeat by the king, loss of wealth, poor food, and constant quarrels with enemies. (21)
Likewise, there will be loss in the morning, suffering, distress, and quarrels;
everything thought of will be fruitless during the sub-period of the Guru.
The death of the master, as well as suffering, loss of wealth, great fear, physical infirmity, quarrels, and terror shall occur during the sub-period of Saturn. (23)
During the sub-period of Mercury, there will occur the total destruction of intellect, loss of wealth, fever in the body, and the ruin of clothing, food, and friends. (24)
During the sub-period of Ketu, there may be laziness, headache, diseases resulting from sinful acts, untimely death, fear of the king, and injury by weapons. (25)
From the Cāṇḍāla [sub-period], there will be distress from narrow passages, fear, and apprehension regarding royal edicts;
furthermore, diarrhea and vomiting will occur during the sub-sub-period of Bhṛgu.
In every transit of the Sun, a person attains the acquisition of land, the fulfillment of goals, contentment, association with friends, and happiness everywhere. (27)
In the southern direction there will be gain, such as white garments and ornaments;
during the sub-period of the Moon, there shall be the successful accomplishment of all undertakings.
Bondage, various diseases, many injuries, and fear from friends—these are to be known as the results during the sub-period of Rāhu within the period of Rāhu. (29)
During the sub-period of Jupiter within the major period of Rāhu, a person obtains honor everywhere, as well as elephants, horses, and the arrival of wealth. (30)
During the sub-period of Saturn, there occurs terrible bondage, the loss of happiness, great fear, and daily affliction from wind-related ailments. (31)
There is gain everywhere in many ways, especially from association with women; success arising in foreign lands will occur within the sub-period of Mercury.
Loss of intellect, fear, obstacles, loss of wealth, and great terror, along with conflict and agitation everywhere—these are the results during the sub-period of Ketu. (33)
During the sub-period of Śukra, there shall be fear of yoginīs, loss of horses, poor food, the death of a wife, and grief arising from one's kinsmen. (34)
Fever, great fear, suffering for one's sons, grandsons, and others, untimely death, and negligence shall occur during the sub-period of Ravi (the Sun). (35)
Agitation, quarrel, anxiety, loss of honor, and great fear;
as well as physical infirmity in the father—these occur during each sub-period (pratyantara) of Jupiter and the Sun. (36)
The results during the sub-period of Mars are: suffering caused by fistula, affliction from hemorrhaging and bile disorders, loss of wealth, and great anxiety. (37)
Gain of gold, increase of grain, auspiciousness, and the arising of good results—these shall be the fruits during the sub-period of Jupiter within the period of Jupiter. (38)
There will be the acquisition of cattle, land, and horses, as well as all means for happiness;
indeed, there will be a collection of food, drink, and other necessities during the sub-period of Saturn. (39)
During the sub-period of Mercury, there will be the acquisition of knowledge, the acquisition of clothing, the acquisition of wisdom along with pearls, and affectionate meetings with friends. (40)
O twice-born one, during the retrograde period of Ketu, there occurs fear of water, theft, imprisonment, quarrels, untimely death, and terrible danger. (41)
During the sub-period of Venus, people attain various branches of knowledge and wealth, as well as gold, clothing, and ornaments;
they obtain security and contentment. (42)
In every solar revolution, a person obtains gain from the king, as well as from friends, father, or even mother,
and receives honor everywhere.
O twice-born one, during the interval of the moon, there is liberation from all suffering and the attainment of freedom for the horse; all undertakings become successful.

During the sub-period of Mars within the major period of Saturn, there will be fear of weapons, suffering from diseases, intoxication by fire, indigestion, and great affliction caused by enemies. (45)
There will be conflict with a Cāṇḍāla, fear from them, and loss of wealth;
suffering within the life-span must certainly be known to occur during the sub-period of Rāhu.
There will be bodily affliction, fear of the Kali age, and dread of the outcaste classes;
various sufferings will arise within the sub-period of Saturn, and [specifically] during the sub-sub-period of Saturn. (47)
When Mercury is in the Pratyantara-dvādaśāṃśa, there is loss of intellect, fear of the Kali age, deficiency in food, drink, and other necessities,
loss of wealth, and fear of enemies.
In the sub-period of Ketu within the major period of Rāhu, there will be imprisonment, birth in an enemy's house, loss of caste, great hunger, anxiety in the mind, fear, and terror. (49)
O twice-born one, whatever virtuous thing is intended always bears fruit for one's own kin; likewise, gain comes from human effort within the intermediate period, O Bhṛgu.
Royal splendor and authority shall arise in one's own home, yet strife and affliction by diseases such as fever will occur during the sub-period of the Sun. (51)

When Saturn is in the sub-period of the Moon, one possesses expanded intellect and undertakes great enterprises, yet has little luster and incurs much expenditure; there is enjoyment together with many women.
During the sub-period of Mars, there will be loss of luster, the death of a son, fear of fire, danger from enemies, and suffering caused by wind and bile disorders. (53)
Loss of wealth, loss of clothing, loss of land, and fear shall occur;
there will be travel to foreign lands or death during the sub-period of Saturn within the major period of Rāhu. (54)

Indeed, one who is incapable of perceiving the aperture (cidra) accepted within the houses, or alternatively, one who speaks of agitation (udvega) toward the preceptor in another context, [is such a person]. 55.
Intelligence, the acquisition of knowledge or wealth, the gain of clothing, and great happiness shall occur during the sub-period of Mercury within the major period of Mercury. (56)
The acquisition of solid food and the occurrence of disease in the stomach, as well as jaundice and hemorrhaging from the bile, may occur during the sub-period of Ketu. (57)
There will be gain from the north, but there may be loss from quadrupeds;
there will be employment in the royal palace during the period opposite to that of Bhṛgu.
When Mercury is in the sub-period of the Sun, there may be a loss of luster, illness, physical suffering at some time or other, and mental instability. (59)
During the Pratyantara period of the Moon, a person obtains the gain of a wife, the attainment of wealth, the birth of a daughter, and great riches;
they obtain happiness from every quarter. (60)

During the sub-period of Mars within the major period of Saturn, there will be the attainment of wealth through religious knowledge, affliction from thieves, fire, and the like, as well as red garments and injury by weapons. (61)
O twice-born one, quarrels arise with women, and danger occurs suddenly; there is fear caused by kings or weapons from enemies within the vicinity. 62.
Sovereignty, or the authority of a kingdom, honor arising from royalty, and the abundance of knowledge and intellect shall come about within a single *pratyantara* of the Guru. (63)
During the sub-period of Saturn, a person suffers from great afflictions of wind and bile, physical injury, and incurs the loss of wealth. (64)
The sudden occurrence of calamities, meeting with someone from another country, and the loss of wealth shall occur during the sub-period of Ketu within the major period of Ketu. || 65 ||
During the sub-period of Venus, there may be fear of barbarians, loss of wealth, eye disease, headache, and the loss of quadrupeds. (66)
Conflict with friends, a slight death, defeat, loss of intellect, and disputes will occur during the sub-period of the Sun. (67)
Loss of food, loss of reputation, bodily affliction, confusion of mind, and an increase in disorders such as āmavāta may occur when there is an eclipse of the Moon. (68)
During the sub-period of Mars, there will be affliction from the blow of a weapon, from a fall, or from the torment of fire;
there will be fear of base persons and apprehension of an enemy. (69)
There shall be great fear from lustful women as well as from enemies;
there may also be fear even from a lowly person, and it shall occur at every change of the moon (pratipada).
Loss of wealth, great calamities, and the destruction of weapons and friends—one experiences suffering everywhere; such is the result when the Sun is in the *pratyantara-daśā* of Jupiter. 71.
The death of cows, buffaloes, and other livestock, physical suffering, the loss of friends,
and the acquisition of very meager gains are the results during the sub-period (pratyantara) of Saturn.
Loss of intellect, great agitation, loss of knowledge, and great fear occur; for the wise man, success in his undertakings does not arise, and the result appears in the next birth. (73)

When the interval of Śukra (the planet Venus) has arrived, and during its sub-interval (pratyantara), a person obtains the happiness born of divine women, consisting of white horses, garments, pearls, and other such luxuries. || 74 ||
Wind-fever, headache, and affliction from the king or even from enemies occur; there is also very little gain—such is the result during the sub-period of the Sun. (75)
During the sub-period of the Moon, there will be the birth of a daughter, gain from the king accompanied by clothing and ornaments, and the attainment of authority over a kingdom. (76)
O twice-born one, during the period of Mars, there may occur diseases such as hemorrhaging (raktapitta), quarrels, and physical assault; moreover, great suffering shall arise. (77)
During the sub-period of Rāhu, quarrels with women arise unexpectedly, there is the occurrence of fear, and suffering from kings and enemies may occur. (78)
Great wealth, a vast kingdom, ornaments such as garments and pearls, and the attainment of elephants, horses, and high rank shall come about during another period of the Guru. (79)
During the sub-period of Saturn, a person obtains donkeys, camels, goats, iron, beans, sesame seeds, and so forth, and experiences only slight suffering. (80)
There will be great gain of wealth and knowledge, and the attainment of kingship and royal power;
furthermore, through the depositing of funds, the wise man shall obtain wealth in another region. (81)
O twice-born one, during the sub-period of Ketu within the middle period, one should know there is fear of untimely death and travel from one country to another; yet, gain also arises in the interim.
Now begins the chapter on the subtle sub-periods (sūkṣmāntardaśā). 62.
The duration of each sub-period (pratyantara-daśā) is obtained by multiplying the years of its own period by the [respective] qualities (guṇa);
this result, divided separately by sixty, shall be the precise sub-period. || 1 ||
When the Sun is in its own subtle transit (nijasūkṣmagati), there may be the abandonment of one's native land, fear for one's life, loss of position, and great loss. || 2 ||
Devotion to the gods and Brahmins, as well as constant engagement in obligatory rites, great affection, and being a friend to all—these occur when the Moon is in the subtle transit of the Sun. (3)
When Mars is in its subtle transit (sūkṣmagati) in the sign of the Sun, there is an inclination toward cruel deeds, oppression by fierce enemies, and diseases such as hemorrhaging and the like.

Fear of thieves, fire, and poison; defeat and rout in battle; and being devoid of charity, righteousness, and other virtues—these indeed occur when the Sun is in its subtle transit through the sign of Aries.
When Jupiter is situated in the subtle transit of the Sun, one is honored by the king, worthy of royal favor, worshipped by servants, regarded with the king's own eyes, and remains tranquil.
When Saturn is in its subtle transit in the Sun's sign, there is theft, acts of violence, harm to gods and Brahmins, displacement from one's position, and mental distress.
When Mercury is in its subtle transit within the [period] of the Sun, there is the attainment of divine garments and other luxuries, the enjoyment of celestial women,
and the accomplishment of unthought-of goals.

When Ketu is in the subtle transit of the Sun, there is the destruction of one's elders and wealth, as well as trouble from servants, wife, and children; in some cases, there may also be a connection with a servant.
When Venus is in its subtle transit (sūkṣmagati) in the Sun's sign, one is indeed endowed with sons, friends, wife, and other such kinsmen, as well as various kinds of prosperity.
Ornaments, the acquisition of land, honor, worship by kings, darkness, goodness, and dignity [are attained] when the Moon is in its own subtle transit. (11)
When Mars is in a subtle transit within the Moon's division, there is suffering, conflict with enemies, abdominal disease, the death of the father, and an aggravation of wind, bile, and phlegm.
When the Moon is in its subtle transit through the sign of Aries, there is anger toward friends and kinsmen, exile from one's country, loss of wealth, and the acquisition of fetters while abroad.
When Jupiter is in the subtle transit of the Moon, one attains prosperity accompanied by whisks and chowries, the wealth of sons, and happiness everywhere.
There will be fear of oppression by the king, loss of wealth in legal disputes, and danger from thieves and Brahmins when Saturn is in the subtle transit of the Moon. (15)
When Mercury is in the subtle transit of the Moon, there is royal honor, the acquisition of wealth, vehicles and the like from foreign lands, and prosperity through sons and grandsons.

When the Dhvaja (flag) is in its subtle transit in the Moon, there will be the destruction of one's livelihood by means of crops, horns, bulls, and the like, as well as fear from fire, the sun, and other such sources.
Marriage, acquisition of land, the splendor of garments and ornaments, attainment of sovereignty, and fame—these occur when Venus is in the subtle transit of the Moon. (18)

From affliction arises further affliction, the destruction of undertakings, the loss of cattle, grain, and wealth, physical deformity, and distress on the land— such are the effects when the Sun is in the subtle transit of the Moon.
When Mars is in its own subtle period (sūkṣmagati), there is loss of land, mental exhaustion, epilepsy, and association with kinsmen; furthermore, there is agitation in the city and mental distress.
When Mars is in the Sūkṣma state during the sub-period of Saturn, there is injury to the limbs, fear of people, the destruction of the wife's lineage,
and a terrible danger from fire and serpents.
When Jupiter has entered the subtle period (sūkṣmagata) of Mars, there is a delight in worshipping the gods, devotion to the recitation of mantras, honor in the world, and great joy.
When Saturn enters the subtle transit of Mars, one who is bound is released from bondage; there is an abundance of wealth, grain, and gifts, along with many servants and great prosperity.
When Mercury is in a subtle transit within Mars, there is happiness associated with vehicles and devoted to royal enjoyments; however, there is also suffering from lust, asthma, and other ailments.

When the banner (the planet Jupiter) is situated in the earth sign (Taurus or Libra) and is in its subtle motion, it causes the intellect to be dependent on others and is censured everywhere; one remains impure at all times.
When Venus enters the subtle transit of Mars, there is the attainment of desired women and enjoyments, the acquisition of desired food, and the gain of desired wealth.

When the Sun is in a subtle transit in the earth element (Bhūmi), one incurs hatred from the king, suffering from Brahmins, and deception regarding one's undertakings; one also falls into reproach in the world.
When the Moon enters the subtle division (sūkṣmabhāga) of Mars, there is purity, the acquisition of wealth, and affection for gods and Brahmins; yet one may be overcome by disease.
There will be a tendency to cause trouble for the world, confusion of intellect in all undertakings, and a sense of emptiness as a defect of mind, even regarding one's own subtle faults. (29)
When Jupiter is in a subtle transit of Rahu, one becomes chronically ill and poor, yet beloved by all; such a person is praised for being devoted to charity and righteousness.

When Saturn is in the subtle transit of Rāhu, one follows evil paths, pursues contemptible goals, serves wicked masters, possesses a mind inclined toward the company of the unrighteous, and is deluded.
When Mercury is in its subtle transit (sūkṣmagati), there is a desire for sexual union with women, eloquence, being surrounded by public acclaim, a longing for food, and physical exhaustion.
Sweetness, loss of honor, bondage,
lack of progeny, harshness, and loss of life occur when Rāhu is in a subtle transit in the sign of Dhvaja (Sagittarius).

One who is bound is released from bondage; there is gain of position, honor, and accumulation of wealth; and there is the acquisition of property through some cause when Venus has entered the subtle transit of Rāhu.
Manifest hemorrhoids, abdominal tumors, and likewise the loss of anger, as well as all happiness from vehicles and other such things, occur when the Sun is in the subtle transit of Rāhu. (35)

When the Moon is in the subtle transit of Rāhu, there is the acquisition of jewels, gems, and wealth; one becomes devoted to the practice of knowledge and virtuous conduct, and intent upon the worship of the gods with devotion. (36)
When Mars is in a subtle transit within Rāhu's division, there is defeat, flight from people, anger toward others, imprisonment, and a constant inclination toward the habit of theft.

When Jupiter enters its subtle transit (sūkṣmagati) in its own sign, there is the destruction of grief, an abundance of wealth, performance of the Agnihotra sacrifice, worship of Śiva, and the acquisition of a vehicle accompanied by an umbrella.
When Saturn is in the subtle transit (sūkṣmagati) of Jupiter, there occurs the breaking of vows, mental anguish, loss of wealth while living in a foreign land,
and conflict with one's kinsmen.
When Mercury is in the subtle transit of Jupiter, there is an increase in knowledge and intellect, the acquisition of wealth with honor,
and every kind of happiness in the home.

Knowledge, wealth, scholarship, listening to the scriptures, worship of Śiva, the Agnihotra sacrifice, devotion to the guru, and [service] when the guru’s subtle banner has set—[these are the duties]. (41)
Liberation from disease, happiness, enjoyment, the acquisition of wealth and grain,
and the joy of children, wife, and so forth— these occur when Venus is in the subtle transit of Jupiter.

There is an aggravation of wind and bile, as well as a severe excess of phlegm; and when the Sun is in the subtle transit of Guru, there is colic caused by the corruption of the bodily fluids and so forth. (43)

When the Moon is in the subtle transit of Jupiter, there is the splendor of wealth accompanied by whisks and chowries, as well as the abundance of sons; however, there is suffering located in the eyes and the belly.
When Mars is in its subtle motion (sūkṣmagati), there is the production of poison from traveling on foot, imprisonment, injury, fear, wandering to another country, and delusion. (45)
One will be overcome by diseases, wealth will be stolen by thieves,
and there will be fear of snakes and scorpions when the Sun is in its subtle transit in the house of the Guru.

Loss of wealth, a major illness, affliction by wind (vāta), and the decay of the family—these occur when Saturn transits its own subtle period (sūkṣmaga) while being afflicted by a break in diet and great suffering. (47)
When Mercury is in the subtle transit of Saturn, there is profit from trade, the acquisition of knowledge and wealth, the gain of a wife, and the attainment of land.

When Saturn is in the subtle transit of the banner (dhvaja), there is affliction from thieves, disturbances, leprosy and other diseases, loss of livelihood, distress, and pain throughout the entire body. 49.
When Venus is in its subtle transit within Saturn's period, there is the attainment of sovereignty, practice with weapons, the birth of a son, consecration, health, and the desire for wealth.
When the Sun enters the subtle transit of Saturn, there arises a transformation of royal splendor within one's own home, yet some suffering arising from one's own body also occurs. (51)

When the Moon is in its subtle transit in the sub-period of Saturn, one possesses expanded intellect and undertakes great enterprises, yet has diminished luster and incurs much expenditure; there is happiness together with wife and children.
When Mars is in a subtle transit within Saturn's period, there occurs a loss of luster, great agitation, weak digestion, dizziness, strife, and suffering caused by wind and bile.
The death of one's father or mother, mental anguish, expenditure regarding elders, and failure in all endeavors occur when Saturday is in its subtle transit. (54)
When Jupiter is in the subtle transit of Saturn, there is honor through the enjoyment of the six seals, an increase in wealth and grain, and the acquisition of the royal parasol and fly-whisk.
When Mercury is in its own subtle transit, there is good fortune, honor from kings, abundance of wealth, grain, and other riches, and one becomes pleasing to behold to all.

When Ketu is in a subtle transit during the period of Mercury, one suffers from fear of children, seizures, and fire; one is afflicted by the defects arising from women's diseases, follows an evil path, and consumes contemptible food.
When Venus is in its subtle transit (sūkṣmagata), there is the acquisition of vehicles, wealth, prosperity, and gains from aquatic products;
there is auspicious fame and great enjoyment.
When the Sun enters the subtle transit of Mercury, there is beating, royal injustice, mental confusion, and susceptibility to disease; furthermore, there is loss and public censure.

When the Moon has entered the subtle state (sūkṣmagati) during the period of Mercury, one becomes fortunate, firm-minded, and endowed with royal honor and wealth; there is also the frequent movement of friends and elders.
When Mars has entered the subtle state during the period of Mercury, there occurs fire-related burns, the arising of poison, dullness, poverty, delusion, and great agitation.

During the sub-period of Mercury, even when the year has reached its subtle stage, there is fear of fire, snakes, and kings; defeat by wicked enemies and the like; and delusion arising from possession by spirits or mental confusion.
When Jupiter has reached the subtle state within the sign of Cancer, there is the acquisition of excellent household utensils, gifts, wealth such as enjoyments,
and the attainment of royal favor.
When Saturn is in the subtle transit of the sign of Mercury, there is the attainment of a livelihood through trade, as well as the wealth of knowledge, the acquisition of a wife, and great success.
When the subtle Jupiter is in its own sign, there is suffering arising from wife and children, physical ailments, poverty, and the livelihood of a mendicant. (65)
When Venus is in its subtle transit (sūkṣmagati), there is the destruction of disease, the acquisition of wealth, affection for teachers and Brahmins, and reunion with one's kinsmen. (66)
When the Sun is in the subtle transit of Ketu, there is war, destruction of land, exile from one's own country, and distress caused by the death of friends.
When the Moon is in a subtle transit within Ketu, there is an abundance of male and female servants, as well as acquisitions in battle and victory; thus, charming fame arises.

When Mars is in the subtle transit of Ketu, there is fear regarding one's seat, affliction from horses, thieves, and wicked persons, as well as suffering from abdominal tumors and diseases of the head. (69)
There is destruction of women and elders due to association with wicked women;
and there is vomiting, blood, and bile when Ketu is in a subtle state even though the Sun is not present.
When Jupiter enters the subtle transit of Ketu, there is conflict with enemies, the acquisition of wealth, sudden royal splendor, and distress from the loss of cattle and fields.
False suffering, birth from a lowly womb, emaciation,
conflict with women, and loss of truthfulness occur when Saturn is in the subtle transit of Ketu.

When Mercury is in the subtle transit of Ketu, there is the acquisition of various kinds of people, separation [from loved ones], affliction from enemies, and the abundant increase of wealth and prosperity.
When Venus is in one's own subtle transit (sūkṣmagati), there is the destruction of enemies, great happiness, the construction of a temple for Śaṅkara, and the excavation of tanks and wells.
When the Sun is in the subtle transit of Venus, there is burning pain in the chest, dizziness, and the restless activity of coming and going; there is gain in some places and loss in others. (75)
When the Moon is in the subtle transit of Venus, there will be health, the attainment of wealth, success in undertakings through coming and going,
and an increase in intellect and learning.
Stupidity, discord with enemies, displacement from one's country, great fear,
and the arising of the suffering of disease occur when Mars is in a subtle transit in the sign of Venus.

Fear of kingship, fire, or serpents, loss of kinsmen, grief for elders, displacement from one's position, and great terror occur even when the subtle planet Rāhu is situated in the sign of Bhṛgu (Vṛścika). (78)
When Jupiter is in the subtle transit of Venus, there is success in all undertakings, the increase of fields, wealth, and prosperity,
and great gains from the profession of trade.
When Saturn is in its subtle transit in the sign of Venus, there will be oppression by enemies, great suffering, the destruction of quadrupeds, and loss to one's own family and preceptors.
When Mercury is in the subtle transit of Venus, there is prosperity among kinsmen and others, legal success, increase of wealth, and happiness derived from children, wife, and so forth. (81)
When the Dhvaja (flag) is in its subtle transit of Bhṛgu, there is disease from fire, great affliction, pain in the face, eyes, and head, and suffering for one who has accumulated wealth.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the Prāṇa-daśā. 63.
One should multiply the subtle period (sūkṣmadaśā) by the years of the respective planet's major period (khagadaśā);
dividing that product by twelve (khasūrya), the quotient obtained should be known as the duration of the sub-period in breath-units (prāṇadaśā). || 1 ||

When the Sun enters the period of Prāṇa, there is suffering during its subtle sub-period (sūkṣmadaśā), including ailments arising from poison, afflictions due to unchastity, and fear caused by thieves, fire, or the king. || 2 ||
When the Moon is in the Prāṇa division of the Sun's Navāṃśa, there is happiness, abundance of food, refinement, and royal splendor, as well as noble qualities and compassion.
When Mars is situated in the Prāṇa-dvāra of the Sun, there is trouble from the king due to other matters, loss of wealth, great fear,
and the occurrence of a major decline.
Great distress regarding food, and especially the outbreak of poisons,
as well as affliction caused by wealth, fire, and kings, occur when the serpent [Rāhu] enters the breath of the Sun.

When Jupiter enters the breath (*prāṇa*) of the Sun during the subtle *āśrama* of the king and the Brahmin, there is the attainment of various branches of knowledge and wealth, and the accomplishment of one's goals through coming and going.
Imprisonment, loss of life, as well as mental agitation,
many afflictions, and great losses occur when Saturn is in the Prāṇa-saṃkrānti of the Sun.
When Mercury is in the *prāṇa* breath of the Sun, one should always enjoy royal food and occupy a position marked by royal insignia; thus one should fully satisfy the self. 8.
When the Dhvaja (the flag) is situated in the Prāṇa of the Sun, there is mutual quarrel, loss of wealth, defeat, and separation from one's teacher, wife, and kinsmen.

When Venus is situated in the Prāṇa-dasha of the Sun, there is honor from the king, an abundance of wealth, happiness arising from wife, sons, and others, as well as the enjoyment of food, drink, and similar luxuries.
When the Moon is in its own Prāṇa-gati, one obtains the happiness of wife, sons, and so forth, wealth, new clothing, yogic perfection, and meditative absorption (samādhi).
When Mars is in the vital breath of the Moon, consumption, leprosy, loss of kinsmen, great danger from hemorrhaging,
and possession by spirits and the like occur.
There will always be specific fears of snakes, disturbances caused by spirits,
agitation of the eyes, and loss of intellect, even when the serpent has entered the vital breath of the moon.
When Jupiter enters the breath of the Moon, there is an increase in righteousness, the attainment of forgiveness, the worship of gods and Brahmins, good fortune, and a pleasing appearance.
When Saturn is in the Prāṇa-saṃkrānti of the Moon, there is a sudden fall from one's body, the pain of an enemy's assault,
blindness, and the acquisition of wealth.

When Mercury is in conjunction with the breath of the Moon, there is the acquisition of a chowrie and an umbrella, followed by the attainment of sovereignty from a king, and equanimity toward all beings. (16)

When the Dhvaja (Jupiter) enters the Prāṇa-dvāra of the Moon, there is suffering caused by weapons, fire, and enemies; affliction from poison and fire; diseases of the stomach; and separation from children and wife. (17)
When Venus has entered the vital breath of the Moon, there is the acquisition of wealth from sons, friends, wife, relatives, and foreign lands; as well as happiness, prosperity, and material gain.
Cruelty, an increase in anger, loss of life, mental anguish,
exile from one's country, and great fear occur when the Sun is in the Prāṇa-saṃkrānti of the Moon.
Quarrels with enemies, imprisonment, and fear of diseases such as hemorrhaging and biliousness—these are the results when Mars enters the vital breath during its own subtle period (sūkṣmadaśā). 20.
Separated from children and wife, and tormented by the calamities of kinsmen,
one may even meet death by poison on the day when the Sun enters the sign of Capricorn.

When Jupiter enters the vital breath of Mars, one becomes devoted to the worship of the gods, endowed with prosperity, intent on the performance of mantras, and attains the happiness of sons and grandsons.
When Saturn enters the vital breath of Mars, there shall be affliction by fire, death, loss of wealth, fall from one's position, and the acquisition of kinsmen through one's relatives. (23)
When Mercury transits the earth-signs (Bhūmiprāṇa), there is the acquisition of divine garments, one is adorned with divine ornaments, and one attains a divine woman. (24)
When the banner (dhvaja) has entered the vital breath of Mars, there is suffering from falls and convulsions, agitation of the eyes, great fear,
and loss of wealth due to snakes.

When Venus has reached the vital breath (prāṇa) of the earth element, there will be abundance of wealth, grain, and other riches, honor from the world, the arrival of happiness, and one will become an enjoyer through various pleasures.
When the Sun is in the Prāṇa-sub-period of Mars, there occurs fever and insanity, loss of wealth arising from the King's displeasure, chronic illness, and poverty. (27)

When the Moon enters the Prāṇa-dasha of Mars, there is the attainment of happiness from food and other comforts, pleasure derived from clothing and ornaments, as well as suffering from cold, heat, and disease.
When Rāhu enters the vital breath (prāṇa), there will be detachment from eating food, fear of poison, and the loss of wealth through rashness. (29)
When Jupiter enters the Prāṇa-dvāra of Rāhu, there is physical comfort, freedom from fear, association with vehicles and commands, loss of status, and the occurrence of quarrels.
When Saturn is in the Prāṇa-dvāra of Rāhu, there occurs a house fire, illness in the body, the loss of wealth by base persons, as well as the occurrence of imprisonment. (31)

When Mercury enters the vital breath of Rāhu, there is the abundance of the teacher’s instruction and the increase of honor for the guru; one becomes possessed of virtues and endowed with good conduct.

When the banner (dhvaja) of Rāhu enters the vital breath (prāṇa), there is conflict with wife, sons, and others, as well as departure from home; furthermore, through rashness, there is loss of the body.
The excellence of a chariot and mount, the accumulation of all desired fruits,
and the commencement of a temple for the worship of Śiva occur when Venus is in the Prāṇa-gati of Rāhu.
When the Sun enters the *prāṇa* breath of Rāhu, there is fear of diseases such as hemorrhoids, the occurrence of royal calamities, and the loss of quadrupeds and other assets. (35)
When the Moon enters the vital breath (prāṇa) of Rāhu, there is cheerfulness, right understanding, respect, the sight of elders, fear of sin, and mental happiness. (36)
When Mars is in the Prāṇa-saṃjñā of Rāhu, there is fear due to the fire of a Cāṇḍāla, loss of one's position,
calamities, impurity, and the livelihood of a dog.

When Jupiter is in one's own Prāṇa-gati, there is the arrival of joy, an abundance of wealth, the performance of the Agnihotra sacrifice, the worship of Śiva, and a vehicle equipped with a parasol. (38)
When Saturn enters the Prāṇa-svara of Jupiter, there is the loss of vows, despondency, loss of wealth in a foreign land, and conflict with one's circle of kinsmen. (39)

When Mercury is in the vital breath of the Guru, there is an increase in knowledge and intellect, honor in the world, the arrival of wealth, and the attainment of happiness through wife, children, and so forth. (40)

Knowledge, worldly prosperity, scholarship, knowledge of the scriptures, worship of Śiva, the Agnihotra sacrifice, devotion to the guru, and [the practice of] the guru’s life-breath as his banner. (41)
Liberation from disease, happiness, enjoyment, the acquisition of wealth and grain,
and the joy arising from children, wife, and so forth— these occur when Venus is in the Prāṇa breath of Jupiter.
When the Sun is in the eighth house from Jupiter, there occurs an aggravation of wind and bile, as well as a severe excess of phlegm,
and colic caused by disorders of the bodily fluids.

When the Moon enters the vital breath (prāṇa) of Jupiter, there is the splendor of wealth accompanied by whisks and chowries, as well as the abundance of sons; yet there is pain located in the eyes and the belly.
When Mars is situated in the eighth house from the Guru (Jupiter), there arises poison from women, imprisonment, severe restraint, wandering to foreign lands, and confusion.
One may be overcome by diseases, one's wealth may be plundered by thieves,
and there may be fear of snakes and scorpions when the planet Saturn enters the *prāṇa* house of the Guru.
When Saturn has reached its own *prāṇa* house, one's luster is scorched by fever, and there may be leprosy, abdominal diseases, and other ailments; death may also occur through water or fire. (47)
When Mercury enters the vital breath of Saturn, there is wealth, grain, auspiciousness, success in business, honor, and devotion to the gods and Brahmins.
When Saturn is in the Dhvaja (the ninth house), there is the suffering of death and disease, the occurrence of calamities from living beings, and the state of being overcome by another's wife.

When Venus enters the Prāṇa-dvāra of Saturn, there is happiness through sons, wealth, and prosperity, as well as comfort from kings and others; furthermore, there is the performance of the Agnihotra sacrifice and marriage.
When the Sun enters the Prāṇa breath during the period of Saturn, there will be pain in the eyes, diseases of the head, fear of snakes and enemies, loss of wealth, and great suffering.
When the Moon enters the vital breath of Saturn, there is health, the birth of a son, the increase of peace, prosperity, and growth, as well as devotion to the gods and Brahmins. (52)
When Mars is in the Prāṇa-dvāra of Saturn, there is abdominal disease, fear of enemies, danger from hunting, destruction of life, and fear of snakes, fire, and poison. (53)
Leaving one's country, fear of the king, delusion, the consumption of poison, and suffering caused by wind and bile occur when the planet Saturn enters the vital breath (prāṇa) during the day. (54)
Generalship, acquisition of land, reunion with kinsmen,
dignity, and honor from the king result when Jupiter is in the Prāṇa-dasa of Saturn.

Health, the attainment of happiness, and the means for accomplishing dharma, karma, and other goals—these belong to the wise man who possesses equanimity toward all beings, as if toward his own life-breath. (56)
When Jupiter is in the Prāṇa-sub-period of Saturn, there is fear from fire and thieves, extreme mental distress, the onset of poison, and suffering that brings about the end of the body. (57)
Sovereignty, abundance of wealth, fame, righteousness, worship of Śiva, happiness regarding children, wife, and so forth—these occur when Venus is in the vital breath of Mercury. (58)
When the Sun has entered the vital breath of Mercury, one experiences internal burning, fever, madness, pleasure from kinsmen, and the acquisition of abundant wealth. (59)

When the Moon enters the vital breath of Mercury, there is the gain of a woman, the attainment of wealth, the acquisition of a daughter, and the arrival of riches; one obtains happiness from every quarter. (60)
When Mars enters the *prāṇa* breath of Mercury, there occurs falling down, diseases of the abdomen, pain arising from the teeth, eyes, and so forth, hemorrhoids, and danger to life.

Abundance of clothing and ornaments, separation [from loved ones], and enmity with Brahmins—such is the suffering arising from the combination of factors when the planet Mercury occupies the vital breath (prāṇa) position on a Saturday. 62.
When Jupiter is in the Prāṇa-saṃjñā of a wise man, there is dignity, wealth, prosperity, learning, the acquisition of excellent virtues,
and gain through industrious effort.
When Saturn transits the vital points of Mercury, there is death by theft, misfortune, poverty, and especially a state of being a beggar. (64)
When the banner of one's own life-force (prāṇa) is struck, there is death by the falling of a horse, conflict with enemies, the onset of quarrels, and the occurrence of an indiscriminate killing. 65.
When Venus is in the Prāṇa-dvāra of Ketu, there is the acquisition of land, the destruction of enemies, the gain of horses, mental happiness,
and the attainment of cattle, fields, and wealth.
Fear of theft, fire, and enemies, loss of wealth, mental anguish, and even life-threatening hardship occur when Ketu is in the Prāṇa-dvāra and the Sun is in the Prāṇa-dvāra. (67)
When the Moon enters the *prāṇa* subdivision of Ketu, there is worship of gods, brahmins, and gurus, long journeys, wealth, and happiness; however, there may be disease in the ear or the eye. (68)
When Mars is in the Prāṇa-dasha of Ketu, there occurs bilious disease, enlargement of the nose, delusion born of the derangement of the three humors (sannipāta), and enmity with one's own kinsmen.
There will be conflict with wife, children, and others, as well as departure from one's home;
due to one's own recklessness, there will be failure in one's undertakings when Ketu is in the Prāṇa-sub-period of the year.
When Jupiter is in the *prāṇa* position of Ketu, there occurs great disease arising from sword-wounds, afflictions such as heartache, and separation from children and wife.

When Ketu is in the Prāṇa-nāḍī and Saturn is in the Āyur-nāḍī, there is confusion and sharpness of intellect, a constant delight in cruel deeds, and suffering due to imprisonment resulting from one's occupation.
Flowers, bedding, ornaments, ointments, food and the like, as well as all forms of physical pleasure to be enjoyed by the entire body, occur when Mercury is in the Prāṇa state of Ketu. (73)
When Venus is situated in its own Prāṇa-dasa, there is knowledge, devotion to the Lord, contentment, the acquisition of wealth, and prosperity through sons and grandsons. (74)

When the Sun has entered the vital breath of Venus, there is fame that illuminates the world, yet one is deprived of the happiness of sons; furthermore, there is suffering born of diseases such as heat-related ailments. (75)

When the Moon enters the vital breath of Venus, one becomes devoted to ritual action in the worship of the gods and intent on pleasing them through mantras; there is an abundance of wealth, good fortune, and prosperity.
When Mars is in the Prāṇa-sub-period of Venus, there is fever, smallpox, eruptions, itching, pustules, and the like; however, there is also worship of the gods and Brahmins.
When the Sun has entered the vital breath of Venus, there is constant suffering caused by enemies, ailments such as eye and stomach diseases,
conflict with friends, and personal distress.
Longevity, health, sovereignty, the prosperity of sons, wife, and wealth, and the acquisition of horses and vehicles [occur] when Jupiter is in the Prāṇa-saṃjñā state of Venus. (79)
Fear arising from royal oppression, loss of happiness, great diseases, and disputes with low-born persons occur when Saturn enters the Prāṇa-dvāra of Venus. (80)
When Mercury is in the Prāṇa-sub-period of Cukra, there will be contentment, honor from kings, prosperity from various regions and lands, and a constant increase in enthusiasm.

When the banner (Jupiter) has entered the vital breath of Venus, there occurs the loss of life, self, and fame, as well as the depletion of wealth and grain; yet there will be generosity, enjoyment, and riches.
Thus, O twice-born one, I have here described before you the results of the planetary periods (daśās) along with their sub-periods (antarās) in brief.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods (antardaśā) of Kālacakra. || 64 ||
I shall now describe those results of the sub-periods within the [planetary] periods which were proclaimed of old by the Enemy of Tripura (Śiva) for the welfare of the world. || 1 ||
When Mars is in its own portion within Aries, there is fever arising from wounds;
when Mercury, Venus, the Moon, or Jupiter are there, there is happiness; and when the Sun is there, there is fear of enemies. (2)
When Saturn enters its own sub-period within the period of Jupiter, there is quarrel and the onset of disease;
however, when Jupiter has entered that [sub-period], the result is the acquisition of knowledge and happiness for the body. (3)
O Brahmin, when Mars enters that [sign], the results are exile from one's country, or death, or a wound from a weapon, or fever. (4)
The acquisition of clothing and ornaments, excellent union with women, and great happiness—these are the results when Venus, Mercury, or the Moon occupy their own Navamsha in Taurus. || 5 ||

When the Sun is in its own Navāṃśa in Gemini, there is fear of the king, the death of a father, and danger from one's own kinsmen and others; yet there is also the acquisition of wealth and clothing through Venus.
Fear for the death of one's father or mother, fever arising from a wound,
and travel to a distant land occur when Mars is in its own Navamsha in the sign of Gemini.
When Jupiter is in its own Navamsha, there is an increase in intellect and learning, the attainment of great prosperity,
honor in the world, and mutual affection between husband and wife.
O Brahmin, when Saturn is in its own Navamsha within the sign of Gemini, there occurs travel abroad, illness, death, loss of wealth,
or the loss of kinsmen.

When Mercury is in its own Navamsha within the sign of Gemini, there is the acquisition of knowledge, clothing, and other such things, as well as happiness arising from wife and children; one attains honor in all respects.
When the Moon is in its own Navamsha in Cancer, there is great happiness from children and wife;
one attains sovereignty in the world, as well as honor and affection. (11)
When the Sun is in its own portion in Cancer, there is fear from enemies and from cattle, as well as from the royal family, and likewise fear of mental anguish and physical disease.
In the Navāṃśa of Mercury and Venus, there is happiness from children, wife, and friends, as well as increase in wealth, honor in the world, and fame. (13)
When Mars is in its own Navāṃśa in Cancer, one experiences fear of death by poison or weapons, the onset of fever and other diseases, and indeed suffers great affliction.
When Jupiter is in its own Navamsha in Cancer, there is an excessive gain of wealth, as well as physical comfort and the attainment of honor from the king. (15)
When Saturn is in its own portion within the sign of Cancer, one encounters terrible fear from the plague of disputes, danger from snakes and scorpions, and various kinds of suffering. (16)
If Mars is situated in its own division within the Leo portion, one should predict fear of diseases of the mouth, affliction caused by bilious fever, or even injury from weapons. (17)
O Brahmin, when Mercury and Venus are situated within their own respective Simhamsas, there is the acquisition of wealth, clothing, and the like, as well as happiness from wife, sons, and others.
When the Moon enters its own sub-period within Leo, there is fear of falling from a height, the acquisition of small amounts of wealth,
and travel to foreign lands.
When the Sun enters the sign of Leo, there is fear from enemies, the onset of diseases such as fever, loss of knowledge, and apprehension of death. (20)
When Jupiter enters the sub-period of Leo, one obtains gains of wealth, grain, and the like, as well as the favor of Brahmins and kings,
and attains an increase in knowledge.
When Saturn is situated in its own portion within the sign of Virgo, a human being encounters hardship, fever, and likewise distress born of hunger. (22)
When Jupiter is in its own Navāṃśa in the sign of Virgo, one obtains the favor of the king, sovereignty, reunion with friends and kinsmen, and growth in knowledge.
When Mars is in its own sub-period within the Kanyā Dasa, there is suffering arising from bilious fever, travel to a foreign land, injury by weapons, and fear of fire. (24)

There is the acquisition of servants, sons, and wealth, as well as the attainment of various pleasures, when Mercury, Venus, and the Moon occupy their respective portions within the sign of Virgo. (25)
When the Sun is in its own portion within the Kanyā Navāṃśa, there is travel, fear of disease, quarrels with kinsmen, and even the danger of being struck by weapons. (26)
If Venus is within Tula, there will certainly be right understanding, the dawning of happiness, and the certain acquisition of women, sons, wealth, new garments, and so forth. || 27 ||
When Mars enters its own sub-period within Libra, there is suffering for one's father, enmity with friends, diseases of the head, the onset of fever,
and fear of poison, weapons, and fire.
When Jupiter occupies its own portion in the sign of Libra, there is the acquisition of wealth, gems, and the like, as well as religious duties, kings, and other honors;
one attains happiness in all respects.
When Saturn is in its own portion in Libra, there will be travel, a major illness, loss of land and other assets,
and harassment from enemies regarding one's undertakings.
The birth of a son, the acquisition of wealth, the pleasure of a wife that is dear to the mind, and the dawn of good fortune are to be recognized when Mercury enters its own period within Libra. (31)
When the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are in Scorpio and situated in their own divisions, there is the acquisition of various grains and wealth, the destruction of disease, and great happiness. (32)
When the Sun is in its own Navāṃśa in Scorpio, one encounters fear of enemies' agitation, disease, loss of wealth, fear of one's father,
and danger from wild beasts.
When Mars is in its own Navāṃśa in Scorpio, one should predict danger from wind and bile, as well as the disease of smallpox,
and fear of fire, weapons, and the like.
When Jupiter is in its own portion in Scorpio, one obtains wealth, grain, jewels, honor from gods and Brahmins, and the favor of the king. (35)
When Saturn is in its own portion within Scorpio, there occurs the destruction of wealth and kinsmen, mental anguish,
affliction from enemies, and a great disease.

When Mars is in its own portion within the sub-period of Saturn, one suffers from excessive burning sensations, fever, vomiting, and especially diseases of the mouth, as well as various other afflictions. (37)

One should predict prosperity, knowledge, good fortune, the destruction of enemies, and happiness from the king when Venus, the Moon, and Jupiter are in their respective portions within the sign of Sagittarius. (38)
When the Sun is situated in its own portion within the sign of Sagittarius (Cāpa), one encounters the loss of wife and wealth, quarrels, fear from the king, and long journeys. (39)
When Jupiter occupies its own portion in Sagittarius, one obtains the fruits of charity, righteousness, and austerity, as well as honor from kings,
and the acquisition of a wife and wealth.
When Saturn is in its own portion within Capricorn, one experiences anger arising from Brahmins, gods, and kings, the destruction of kinsmen, and exile from one's country. (41)

Worship of the gods, austerity, meditation, and honor within the royal family are the results of the sub-period (antardaśā) of Venus, Mercury, the Moon, and Jupiter when they are in the Navāṃśa of the Moon. (42)
When Mars is situated in the portion of Mṛgaśiras, it brings about diseases of the head, fever, wounds to the hands and feet,
as well as hemorrhaging, bilious disorders, and dysentery.

When Saturn is in its own portion within the Mṛga constellation, it brings about the destruction of paternal kinsmen, afflictions such as fever and disease, and even fear of the king and enemies. (44)
When Venus occupies its own portion in the sign Aquarius, there is the acquisition of various branches of knowledge, happiness derived from sons, wife, and friends,
physical health, and prosperity.
When Mars is within the portion of the Ghaṭa-lagna, one suffers affliction from fever, fire, and thieves, as well as great fear from enemies, and experiences mental anguish.
When Jupiter is in its own portion within the portion of Kumbha, one obtains freedom from disease, happiness, honor from the king, and clarity of mind through the twice-born.
When Saturn is in its own portion within the ninth part of Aquarius, one encounters provocation of the three humors, quarrels, regional upheaval, and the affliction of wasting diseases.
When Mercury is in its own portion within the portion of Aquarius, one attains the gain of sons, friends, wealth, and wives that are dear to the mind, as well as an increase in good fortune.

When the Moon is in its own portion within the sign of Pisces, one attains growth in knowledge, the happiness of women, the destruction of disease, the company of friends, and delight of the mind. (50)
When the Sun is in its own portion within the sign of Pisces, one encounters quarrels with kinsmen, fear of thieves, mental anguish, and displacement from one's position. (51)

In the portion of Pisces (Mīnāṃśa), one attains victory in battle, gains cattle, land, and sons, and there is an increase in wealth; this applies to its own portions as well as those of Mercury and Venus. 52.
When Mars occupies its own Navāṃśa within the Pisces Navāṃśa, a person suffers from bile-related diseases, disputes even with his own kinsmen, and faces fear from enemies. (53)
When Jupiter occupies its own portion within the Pisces division, there is the acquisition of wealth, clothing, and a wife; honor from the king, and manifold prestige in the world. (54)
Loss of wealth, mental anguish, and association with courtesans and the like, or even exile from one's country, shall occur when Saturn is in its own portion within the Pisces Navamsha. (55)

Thus should the results of the periods (daśās) of Kālacakra be understood by the wise, as well as the results of the sub-periods (antardaśās); and it is exactly the same even for the odd signs (vāmarkṣa).
This fruit, produced by dharma and adharma in the past, has been declared by me;
all of that is constantly obtained with one's own hands—of this there is no doubt. (57)
O best of the twice-born, the sub-period (antardaśā) of a friend is auspicious even for a malefic planet;
likewise, that of an enemy is declared to be inauspicious even for a benefic planet. (58)
Now begins the chapter on the results of the nine-division periods (*navāṃśa-daśā*) of Kālacakra. || 65 ||
In Aries there is suffering born of blood; in Taurus, an increase in grain;
in Gemini, an increase in knowledge; and in Cancer, one becomes a lord of wealth. (1)
In Leo, there will be affliction from enemies; in Virgo, happiness from women;
in Libra, the status of a royal minister; and in Scorpio, fear of death. (2)
O best of the twice-born, one should know that there will be the acquisition of wealth when the ninth degree of Aries is in the period; such is the result during the time of the dasa.
In Capricorn there are evil deeds; in Aquarius wealth from trade;
in Pisces the accomplishment of all aims; and in Scorpio fear of fire. (4)
In the sign of Libra, there is honor from the king; in Virgo, fear of enemies;
in Cancer, distress for one's wife and family; and in Leo, suffering for the eyes. || 5 ||
In Gemini, there is fear of poison; in the ninth degree of Taurus, there is gain of wealth;
in Taurus itself, there is gain of wealth; but in Aries, there arises fever.
In Pisces there is affection for maternal uncles; in Aquarius, the increase of enemies;
in Capricorn, fear of thieves; and in Sagittarius, the increase of knowledge. || 7 ||
In Aries there is a multitude of weapons, while in Taurus there will be quarrel;
in Gemini one attains happiness—such is the fruit in the portion of Gemini.
In Cancer one attains happiness; in Leo there is fear from the king;
in Virgo there is happiness from kinsmen; and in Libra one shall obtain fame.
In Scorpio there is suffering for the father; in Sagittarius, the acquisition of knowledge and wealth;
in Capricorn, infamy in the world; and in Aquarius, loss through trade. (10)
In Pisces one attains happiness; such is the result in the Cancer division (navāṃśa).
In Scorpio there is quarrel and suffering; in the Libra division, there is happiness and prosperity. || 11 ||
In Virgo, there will be wealth and grain; in Cancer, fear from herds of animals;
in Leo, both happiness and suffering; and in Gemini, an increase in enemies. (12)
In Taurus there is the attainment of happiness; in Aries one shall encounter suffering;
and in Pisces there will be a long journey—such is the fruit in the Leo division (siṃhāṃśa).
In the sign of Aquarius (Kumbha), there shall be gain of wealth; in Capricorn (Makara) as well, the arrival of wealth;
in Sagittarius (Dhanu), happiness from one's brothers; and in Aries (Meṣa), one should predict happiness from one's mother.
In Taurus, there is happiness from sons; in Gemini, fear from enemies;
in Cancer, affection with wife and kinsmen; and in Leo, an increase in disease. (15)

The birth of a son from a daughter, and such results as these, occur when the portion of Virgo is [ascendant]; in Libra there is abundance of wealth, and in Scorpio there is happiness from brothers. (16)
One should declare happiness from the paternal side in Aries, suffering for one's mother in Taurus;
gain from trade in Aquarius, and happiness and prosperity in Pisces. (17)
In Scorpio there is suffering for women, and in Libra there is fear from water;
in Virgo there is happiness and prosperity—such is the result in the portion of Libra.
In Cancer there will be loss of wealth; in Leo, fear from the king;
in Gemini, gain of land; and in Taurus, abundance of wealth. (19)
In Aries, however, there is suffering born of blood; in Pisces, one should predict happiness.
In Aquarius, there is profit from trade; and in Capricorn, there is loss of wealth. (20)
In Sagittarius, there is the attainment of happiness; this is the result in the portion of Scorpio.
In Aries, there will be the gain of wealth, and in Taurus, the increase of land.
In Gemini, there shall be the attainment of all success; in Cancer, the abundance of happiness;
in Leo, the arising of all pleasures; and in Virgo, the onset of quarrels. || 22 ||
In Libra, there will be profit from trade; in Scorpio, fear arising from illness;
and in Sagittarius, the happiness of having sons—such are the results to be declared for the Dhanu (Sagittarius) division. (23)
In Capricorn there shall be the gain of a son; in Aquarius, the increase of wealth;
in Pisces, one attains auspiciousness; and in Scorpio, fear from animals.
In Libra there will be the acquisition of wealth; in Virgo, fear from enemies;
in Cancer, one attains prosperity; and in Leo, fear from enemy people. (25)
In Gemini, there is fear of poison; such is the result in the portion of Cancer. In Taurus, there is abundance of wealth; in Aries, there is the danger of eye disease. (26)
In the sign of Pisces, there will be long journeys; in Aquarius, the increase of wealth;
in Capricorn, the attainment of all success; and in Sagittarius, the increase of knowledge. (27)
In Aries there shall be the destruction of happiness; in Taurus, death may occur;
in Gemini, there is the attainment of happiness and prosperity—such is the fruit in the Kumbha division. 28.
In Cancer there shall be an increase of wealth; in Leo, one should predict patronage from the king;
in Virgo, wealth and grain; and in Libra, wealth from trade. (29)
In Scorpio, there is suffering born of fever; in Sagittarius, the dawning of knowledge and happiness;
in Capricorn, there will be conflict with women; and in Aquarius, danger from water. (30)
In Pisces, there is total auspiciousness; such is the result in the Pisces portion.
Having understood [the results] according to the sequence of the first degrees of the decans, one should declare all the results.
During the period of a malefic planet, one should perform propitiatory rites according to the prescribed rules;
thereby, one will undoubtedly obtain auspicious results during that period. || 32 ||
Now begins the chapter on the Aṣṭakavarga. 66.
O Blessed One, you have explained the results arising from the states of the planets and so forth, which is approved by many excellent sages and teachers. (1)

Because of the confusion regarding their results and the confusion in the movements of the planets, not all men are capable of speaking with certainty, saying, "It is exactly thus," once they have understood [the matter]. (2)
In this Kali age, the intellect of men is joined with a predilection for sin;
therefore, please explain to me this scripture which is accessible even to those of limited intelligence. (3)
Through the specific positions of the planets at various times, there is a clear discernment of the happiness and suffering of human beings, as well as a determination of their lifespan.
Well asked by you, O Brahmin; I shall speak before you concerning the thorough knowledge of the conduct of the world, as well as the determination of the lifespan.
Listen with an attentive mind to the non-contradiction regarding intermixture and the purpose of the scripture as well, for the sake of benefiting people. (6)
The houses from the ascendant (lagna) up to the twelfth (vyaya) yield results according to their respective names;
they are considered auspicious when aspected by or joined with benefic planets. || 7 ||

Those houses, when not aspected by or conjoined with malefic planets situated in exaltation and other such favorable divisions, nor with those in debilitation, enemies' signs, or fall, bestow results that are auspicious rather than otherwise. || 8 ||
"By those situated in their own, exaltation, or friendly signs, and not in their fall or inimical signs;
thus has it been stated in general by the wise masters learned in the science of horā. (9)
All this has been declared by me, following in the footsteps of the ancient teachers;
longevity and the conduct of worldly life are the purpose of this treatise. (10)
Neither Vasiṣṭha nor Bṛhaspati is able to determine that;
how much less so can human beings, especially in the Kali age? (11)
The science of astrology (jyotiḥśāstra) is declared to be twofold: the general portion and the specific portion.
The general part has been explained; now the definitive portion is being described. (12)

Just as the results arising from the houses for the planets are determined from the ascendant and the moon, so too should they be considered by the best of astrologers from the other planets as well. (13)

Therefore, for the eight planets beginning with the Sun along with the ascendant, the respective inauspicious and auspicious results arising from all the houses should be determined individually as previously described. (14)

Having first understood the instrument and its location, characterized by the *bindu* and the line (*rekhā*), the clear results of the eightfold division (*aṣṭakavarga*) should be declared in due order. (15)
In the third, sixth, and eleventh houses, there are three; in the seventh and fourth, five; in the fifth and twelfth, four;
in the sixth, ninth, and second, three; in the third, tenth, and eighth, six; and in the first and ninth, one. (16)
The Ascendant, Moon, Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and Saturn are situated in the first house;
the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Moon, and Jupiter are in the twelfth house; and Mercury, Moon, Venus, and Saturn are in the second house. (17)
In the house of happiness (the second), the lords of the hora, the Moon, and Venus [are the significators]; in the house of dharma (the ninth), the Sun, Saturn, and Mars;

in the house of enemies (the sixth), the lord of the hora, Jupiter, and the Moon; in the house of desire (the seventh), the one worshipped by the lord of the Daityas (Venus); and in the house of existence (the fifth), [the same]. 18.
In the Sahaja [house], there are the Sun, Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, and Mars; in the Khe [the tenth house], Jupiter and Venus;
in the Suta [fifth house], the Sun, Saturn, Moon, the Ascendant, Mars, and Venus. This is the Karaṇa of the Sun. (19)

In the houses of fortune (the second) and self (the tenth), there are six; in the houses of death and the hora, five; in the houses of honor (the third) and the fifth house, one; in the houses of children (the fifth) and wisdom (the fourth), four; and in the houses of enemies (the sixth) and women (the seventh), [three]. (20)
For the Moon, however, there are three [points] in the twelfth, eighth, and eleventh houses, and zero in the others;
the lords of the periods are Mars, the Sun, Rāhu, Saturn, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, Saturn, and Venus. (21)
Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, and the Ascendant; Hōra, the Moon, Jupiter, and the Sun; Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter; Mars, the Ascendant, Saturn, and those two, Venus and the Moon. (22)
The lords of the hour (Lagna), Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, and the void (Rāhu) are, in order, the [planetary] strengths in the twelfth, second, fifth, and seventh houses;
six and seven are the strengths in the second and ninth houses respectively. (23)
In the case of Horā and Mṛtyu, the values are five and four; in Vikrama, they are zero; in Kṣata, three;
in Bhava, two; and in Śūnya, likewise zero—such is the calculation for Mars.
Mars, the Sun, the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the Ascendant, and Saturn; Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—these are the lords of the houses mentioned for Dharma, with the exception of Mars. (25)
Candra, Arka, Guru, Śukra, Ārki, and Lagna; Kuja and Bhāskara; Jña, Indu, Arka, Sita, Lagna, and Ārya—among these, excluding Śukra [from the latter group]. (26)

Excluding Saturn, there are seven [planets] in the Dharma [division]; Venus, the Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, then [Saturn], the Sun, Mars, Mercury, the Moon, the Ascendant, and Mars; these are declared as the Karaṇas in sequence. (27)

The digits for the houses are as follows: one for the self, three for the house, two for karma, seven for enemies, three for dharma, three for Agni (the fourth), five for Mṛga (the fifth), two for hands (the sixth), six for brothers, six for wife, zero for gain, zero for children, and five for expenditure. (28)
For Mercury, the lords of the houses starting from the ascendant are, in order: Mercury, Sun, Moon, Jupiter, Jupiter, Sun, Mercury, and Saturn; for the Sun, they are:
Ascendant, Sun, Mars, Saturn, Moon, Jupiter, Mercury, and Saturn; and for Venus, they are: Mercury, Sun, Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, Sun, Jupiter, and Venus. (29)
Jupiter, Moon, Sun, Ascendant; Venus, Mars, Saturn;
Mercury, Moon, Ascendant, Sun, Venus, Jupiter; Mercury, Sun; Jupiter, Moon, Ascendant. || 30 ||
The Sun, Jupiter, and Venus [occupy] zero; Mercury, the Moon, Mars, Saturn, and Venus [occupy] one;
in the second and third houses [they occupy] two; in the twelfth house seven; and in the eighth house four. (31)
In the houses of death (the eighth) and valor (the tenth), five planets are unfavorable for the Guru; in the remaining houses, they are as many as fire (three).
Venus, the Moon, and Saturn are unfavorable in the ascendant; Saturn alone is unfavorable in its own house and in the eleventh house; and Saturn is also unfavorable in the tenth house.
Mars, the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus are in the house [of the ascendant];
Mercury, Saturn, and Mars are in the seventh house; and Venus, Saturn, and the Moon are in the tenth house; while Mercury, Venus, and Saturn are in the [twelfth] house. (33)
Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Sun are all situated in the sixth house; Venus is in the twelfth house, excluding Saturn;
the Moon and Saturn are in the tenth house; and Saturn, Mars, and Jupiter are in the ninth house, while Mercury is in the seventh house. (34)

The ascendant, Saturn, Venus, the Moon, and Mercury [are the lords of the houses]; this is the method for Jupiter. [The numbers] 2, 10, 3, and 1 are for the fifth, eleventh, and third houses; 2, 8, 12, 0, and 5 are for the first, fourth, seventh, tenth, and ninth houses respectively. (35)
In the seventh house (the wife's sign), there are eight; in the fourth, six; in the ninth, one; in the fifth, two; in the tenth, zero; and in the first, zero.
In its own sign, the Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn are all present; and in the seventh house, all [planets] are present. (36)
The Sun and Mars are in the third house; the Sun and Mars are in the fifth house;
the benefics and the Sun are in the fourth house; and Mars and Mercury are in the eighth house, O twice-born one. (37)
Venus, the Sun, the Moon, Mars, the Ascendant, and Jupiter [are the lords] in the sixth house; there is a zero [contribution] in the eighth and twelfth houses.
Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon [are the lords] in the first house; and Mars, Mercury, the Moon, and Venus [are the lords] in the tenth house. (38)

In the houses of one's own wife, death, and the lord of the hour (mṛti-horā), the values are seven and six parts respectively; in the houses of authority, brothers, and the twelfth, they are four; in the house of the enemy, one; and in the house of the son, five. (39)
Thus, when the Sun is in the seventh house and Saturn is in the tenth, this is declared by the wise to be the *karaṇa* known as Āya-śūnya;
likewise, when the Ascendant and the Sun are both in the same house or in the first house, excluding the Sun from its own sign. (40)
Leaving aside the wise [planet] in the Dharma house, one should consider those born from Mars, Saturn, the Sun, and the Moon when they are situated in Māna;
then Jupiter, the Sun, Mercury, and Venus in Bhrātṛ; and the Sun in Kṣata. (41)

In the twelfth house, the Ascendant, Moon, Saturn, and Sun; in the fifth, Venus, Sun, Moon, Mercury, and the Ascendant; in the sixth and eighth, Mercury and Sun; and excluding the tenth house from the positions of Saturn and Mercury. (42)
It has been stated that others are "givers of place"; thus the wise understand *sthāna*.
Now, for the easy understanding of the learned, I shall describe the planets of *sthāna*. (43)
Mandāra, Sūrya, Jīva, and Budha are in the self (ātman); Jña, Indu, and Lagna are in the son (suta);
Jña, Indu, and Lagna are in valor (vikrama); and Lagna, Arka, Arkī, and Kuja are in the house (gṛha). 44.
And those [planets] are in the second house when Jupiter and the Moon are in the tenth; all [are so] except Venus when it is in the twelfth.
When Venus, Mercury, and the Ascendant are in the sixth, as are Jupiter and the Moon. (45)
In the seventh house: the Sun, Mars, Saturn, and Venus; in the tenth: Mars, the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter; in the fourth: Mercury, the Moon, and Jupiter; in the first:
Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus. (46)
Jīva, Śukra, and Budha; Bhauma, Budha, Śukra, and Śanaiścara; Ravi, Indu, Ārā, Arkila, and Lagna; and Ravi, Indu, Āri, Jña, and Bhārgava. (47)
The Sun, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and the Moon, as well as those two, Mars and Saturn, are all said to be in the zero-position (śūnya) respectively; and so too is the position of the Moon. (48)
The Ascendant, Saturn, and Mars; Mars, the Moon, Jupiter, and the Lord of the Day (the Sun);
Saturn and Mars; Mercury and the Sun; Mercury, the Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, the Ascendant, and Venus. (49)
The two Mandāra trees are white; Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and the Sun are the lords of the houses.
All are Jupiter and Venus; the wise know Mars alone to be the place. (50)
Mars, Saturn, Venus, and Mercury; Mars, the Moon, Venus, and Saturn;
Venus and Mercury; Mars, the Moon, the Sun, Venus, and Jupiter; Mercury, the Sun, and Venus. || 51 ||
The soul, Jupiter, the Sun, the Moon, and the Ascendant; Mars and Saturn;
those two [Mars and Saturn] along with the Ascendant and the Moon; Indra (Jupiter), Bṛhaspati (Jupiter), Saturn, Mars, the Sun, Mercury, and Venus. (52)
The Ascendant, Saturn, Venus, and the Moon; all [the others], Jupiter, Mercury, and the Sun;
Jupiter in the Ascendant and the fourth house; Jupiter, Mars, and Mercury in the second house. (53)
The Moon and Venus are in the third house; Saturn, Jupiter, and the Sun are in the twelfth house;
and Venus, the Moon, the Ascendant, Mercury, and Saturn are in the fifth house—except for the Moon, the two [other] planets [Sun and Mars] are there. (54)
If Mars, Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon are in the seventh house; if Saturn, Jupiter, the Sun, and Mars are in the eighth house;
and if Venus, the Sun, the Ascendant, the Moon, and Mercury are in the ninth house—excluding Saturn—from that sign [the results follow]. (55)

They know that the ascendant, Venus, the Moon, Mercury, Saturn, and Jupiter are the *horās* of Mars; likewise, those same [planets] are the *rāśis* of Mercury, the Sun, and Venus, respectively, with the exception of Mercury. (56)
In the *sutabhā* (the fifth house), there are Saturn, Mercury, Moon, Jupiter, Sun, and Venus;
in the *jñārabhā* (the ninth house), there is a void; and in the *sitārkendugurulagnasanaicarāḥ* (the tenth house), there are Venus, Sun, Moon, Jupiter, Ascendant, and Saturn. (57)

All [the planets] except the Sun [are favorable] for Venus; Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars [are favorable] for the sign of honor (Mānabha); and all [the planets] except Mars, the Moon, and the Sun are [favorable] for Mercury, in due order. 58.
In the case of Saturn, the Sun is in the body [the first house]; the Sun, the Ascendant, the Moon, Mars, and Venus;
the Ascendant and the Sun; Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars—all these, with the exception of the Sun, are situated in the wound. (59)
The Sun, Saturn, and Jupiter; Mercury, the Sun, and Mars; and then all [the planets]—Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus—know this sequence of positions. (60)
In the third, fourth, and seventh houses, there shall be three fires; in the second house, two;

in the eleventh, five; and in the houses of the intellect (fifth), death (eighth), and the ninth (apha), there are six in the signs of the lord of the sky (the tenth) and the lord of the eyes (the second).
Having set aside the heavy [planets] among the female signs, this is the calculation for the ascendant:
the Ascendant, Sun, and Moon are in the ascendant; [the lords of] the Ascendant, Sun, Moon, Mars, and Jupiter are [in their respective houses]. (62)

Jupiter and Mercury [are auspicious] in the ascendant; the Moon, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, and Saturn in the fourth house; Venus alone in the seventh house; and all [the planets], excluding Jupiter, in the ninth house. (63)

Leaving aside Mars and Mercury in the second house, Jupiter and Venus excepted from the eleventh house, likewise Venus in the tenth house, and all planets except the Sun and Moon in the twelfth house; 64.
O best of the twice-born, this calculation of the ascendant has been fully explained;
now, O best of the twice-born, I shall describe the positions of the ascendant.
The days of Saturn, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter, and Mars; [the planets] Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus;
excluding Mercury and Jupiter, the remaining ones—Saturn, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus; and the son of the Sun (Saturn). 66.
Likewise, when there is an injury to the intellect (Buddhi), all except Śukra and Jīva are present;
similarly, when there is an injury to the Soul (Jīva), only one [planet] is present; and likewise, when there is an injury to the Sun (Dyūna), Saumya and Bhṛgu are present. (67)

In the tenth house (dharmasthāna) are Jupiter and Venus; in the tenth house (kha) is Mercury; and likewise, the Sun and Moon are situated in the twelfth house (ariṣṭha)—this is declared to be the position of the ascendant. 68.
The *karaṇa* should be drawn like a drop, while the *sthāna* has the nature of a line.
The *karaṇa* is said to bestow inauspicious results, whereas the *sthāna* bestows auspicious fruits. (69)
One should draw ten vertical lines and fourteen horizontal lines;
thus, a wheel consisting of sixty-three squares (nagesha-koṣṭha) is produced.

The wise man should write the numbers representing the houses, joined with the conjunctions, across the eight horizontal compartments; likewise, he should write them in the first vertical compartments, both above and below. (71)
As it has been stated, one should place there either the *karaṇa* or the very position;
then, having understood the auspicious or inauspicious [influences], one should declare the results for the native.
Now begins the sixty-seventh chapter: The Purification of Triangles.
Having thus prepared the Aṣṭakavarga for the planets along with their ascendants, one should first perform the subtraction of trines for all the signs. (1)
O Brahmin, the triangle is said to consist of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius;
likewise, Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn, Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius.
Aries, Scorpio, and Pisces are mutually triangular signs;
one should place the results of the Aṣṭavarga for all the signs below each other.
