Whatever is deficient in the trines should be subtracted equally from all three; however, if there is a zero in one house, one should not subtract it from that trine. || 4 ||
When there is equality across all houses, the wise man should purify everything; thereafter, the learned one should perform the purification of the single lord.
Now begins the chapter on the purification of the single lordship (ekādhipatya). || 68 ||
Having first purified the triangle, one should establish the results of the zodiacal signs;
thereafter, one should perform the purification of the single lords individually. || 1 ||
When there are results in two houses, one should then perform the subtraction as follows:
subtract from the other house that which remains deficient, provided it is devoid of planets.
When there is a conjunction of both [planets], one should never perform a subtraction;
[this applies] when the planet is joined with [a point] lacking results, or when there is an absence of a planet [at the point] while the results are excessive. || 3 ||

If [the result] is less than [the divisor], one should subtract it from the other [value] when that other is devoid of planets; if the result is greater than the planets, one should add the planets to it, and in the other case, one should discard everything.
When there is an absence of planets in both places and they are equal, one should discard everything;
when the presence and absence of planets are equal, everything should be subtracted from the planetless side.
The domains and the respective fruits of the two signs, Cancer and Leo, being distinct,
one should first eliminate their shared lordship and then calculate the total sum.
Now begins the chapter on the calculation of the *piṇḍa* (sum). 69.
In this manner, one should multiply the remaining quotient by the measure of the zodiacal sign;
and when that sign is occupied by a planet, one should further multiply it by the measure of the planet. || 1 ||
Furthermore, O twice-born one, the combined yoga of all these is called Piṇḍa:
Taurus and Leo are multiplied by ten, while Gemini and Scorpio are multiplied by eight.
Libra and Aries are multiplied by seven, and Capricorn and Virgo by five;
the remaining signs are to be multiplied by their own respective numbers. Now, the dimensions of the zodiacal signs are stated. (3)
The measures for Jupiter, the Sun, Venus, and Mercury are ten, eight, seven, and five [years] respectively;
and for the remaining planets, the measure is declared as follows in order. (4)
Now begins the chapter on the results of the Aṣṭakavarga. 70.
The fruit from the Sun is the power of one's own nature and consideration for one's father;
from the Moon, it is clarity of mind and intellect and consideration for one's mother. (1)

One should consider the nature of brothers, virtues, the earth, and matters pertaining to the ground by means of Mars; however, trade, occupation, and friends should be considered by means of Mercury. (2)
Through Guru one obtains nourishment of the body, sacred knowledge, sons, wealth, and prosperity;
through Bhṛgu, marriage rites, objects of enjoyment, places of residence, and vehicles. (3)
One should examine association with courtesans and women through Venus,
as well as longevity, means of livelihood, and sufferings, griefs, and fears.
One should observe the death resulting from the exhaustion of all [karmas] by means of the slow [motion];
one should multiply the aggregate of conjunctions by the numerical value of the fruit of each respective state. (5)
When Saturn moves into a lunar mansion equal to the remainder obtained by dividing [the elapsed days] by twenty-seven,
one should predict affliction for that particular house.
The ninth sign from the sign occupied by the Sun is known as the house of the ancestors (Pitṛgṛha).
One should increase the total sum of the yogas by the number of the results of that sign.
When Saturn enters the remaining asterism after dividing [the zodiac] by twenty-seven, there is suffering for the ancestors; of this there is no doubt.
If [the planet] is situated in the trine (trikoṇa) there, one should know that his father, or even someone like a father, will die; or else, one should predict great suffering.
Or one should multiply the yoga-piṇḍa by the number of the result of that heap;
when the son of the Sun (Saturn) reaches the lunar mansion remaining after being divided by twelve.
If that [planet] is in a trine or its own sign, one should declare paternal suffering;
however, during its period (daśā) which bestows misfortune (riṣṭa), death occurs, whereas at other times there is merely suffering.
If Rāhu or Saturn, or Mars, occupies the fourth house from the Sun, and this occurs without the aspect of Jupiter or Venus, the man becomes a killer of his father. (12)

If Saturn has gone to the position of Jupiter from the ascendant or from the Moon, and is aspected by or conjoined with malefic planets, the wise man should predict the destruction of the father. || 13 ||
During the period of the malefic planet that is the lord of the fourth house from the ascendant, there is destruction of the father;
however, during its favorable period, this does not occur—thus should it be considered by the wise. (14)
One born on the eighth lunar day of the father’s birth, or when its lord is situated in the ascendant, performs the ancestral rites; of this there is no doubt. (15)

During the period (daśā) of the lord of the fourth house, there is the possibility of attaining happiness. If the lord of the fourth house is situated in the ascendant or the eleventh house, especially from the position of the Moon, and is joined with the fourth house, the native will follow the will of his father. || 16 ||
One born in the third lunar mansion from that of one's father is dependent on paternal wealth;
one born in the house of the father’s karma is endowed with qualities equal to those of the father. || 17 ||
Even if that lord [of the sign] is situated in the ascendant, the man will be the best among his paternal kin;
likewise, one should consider here also the general results previously mentioned.
Whatever house is empty in the Sun’s eightfold division (aṣṭavarga),
one should avoid performing auspicious rites such as marriage, vows, and tonsure ceremonies during that month and year.
Where there is an excess of lines, in that month and even in that year,
one may perform auspicious rites even if the Sun and Jupiter are unfavorable.
Likewise, in the Moon’s eightfold division (candrāṣṭavarga), wherever there may be many zeros, when the Moon enters those positions, one should abandon auspicious undertakings. || 21 ||
The fourth from the Moon concerns the contemplation of the village and the favor of one's mother;
it yields the fruit of happiness, increases the *piṇḍa*, and one should enjoy oneself with food.
When Saturn has entered the remaining asterism (Śeṣarkṣa), one should predict the death of the mother;
and when Saturn has gone to its trine from there as well, one should declare illness for the mother.
The strength, valor, and fortitude of a brother are to be considered through the eightfold division (aṣṭavarga) of Mars;
the third sign from the one occupied by Mars is traditionally regarded by the wise as the house of the brother.
Having performed the purification of the triangle, wherever there may be an excess [of points], there is the acquisition of land, a wife, and the highest happiness from brothers. (25)
If Mars is devoid of strength, one will have a long life but be destitute of brothers;
wherever the fruits [of past actions] are exhausted, there is loss when Mars has gone to that place. (26)
Then, having increased the piṇḍa by the fruit of the third asterism as before, one should predict suffering for a brother when Saturn reaches the remaining asterism. (27)
In the fourth house from Mercury, one should consider the family, the maternal uncle, and friends;
when Mercury has entered a sign with abundant results, it bestows happiness upon them.
Having calculated the Budha-aṣṭavarga, when Saturn transits the remaining asterism, one should predict suffering for one's family, friends, and maternal uncles. (29)
One should consider knowledge from the fifth house, and dharma and sons from that [fifth] house; in that sign where the results are predominant, one should predict happiness for one's progeny. (30)

Whatever the number of results that may exist in the position of Bṛhaspati’s son (Mercury), excluding planets that are inimical or in their sign of debilitation, there will certainly be that many offspring. (31)
Or the progeny may be equal to the [planets'] positions in the fifth house and their Navāṃśas;
thus, having multiplied the Piṇḍa by the results of the fifth house as before, [one should proceed]. (32)
One should recognize suffering for one's sons when Saturn has entered the remaining asterism;
thus, one whose mind is darkened by time should calculate both dharma and knowledge.
Having cast the afflicted division of the enemy into the celestial movers, wherever the results may be most abundant, there indeed is the *kali* [period]. (34)
One should determine wealth, wife, and land from the respective houses [of the planets] in that specific region;
the wise should consider the acquisition of a wife from Venus in the seventh house. (35)

The happiness and sorrow arising from the direction and region of the sign situated in the seventh house or its trines should be considered for the woman; the *piṇḍa* should be increased as before. (36)
The eighth house from the sign occupied by Saturn is known as the house of death;
that very same house is the locus of longevity, therefore one should contemplate longevity from it. (37)
One should calculate the results from the ascendant up to Saturn and combine them together;
in the year equal to the sum of those results, one should predict illness and enmity. (38)
In this manner, one should combine the results from the sign of Aries (Manda) up to the ascendant (Lagna) into a single total;
for one born in a year equal to that [total], one should predict the danger of disease. (39)
If the year is equal to the conjunction of two [planets], one should predict suffering equal to death;
when there is a conjunction with the misfortune of a planetary period (daśāriṣṭa), it is death itself, without a doubt. || 40 ||
Having established the *piṇḍa*, one should multiply it by the results of Saturn's eighth-parts;
the asterism traversed by Saturn is equal to the remainder divided by twenty-seven. || 41 ||

One should predict the death of the native when [the Moon] is in that trine or its sign; or one should predict it when the Moon is in the sign of the remainder [of the calculation] from the Sun, or even in its trine. || 42 ||
If there is no auspicious result in the house where Saturn's eightfold division (aṣṭavarga) yields no fruit, then nothing good will happen for him when Saturn enters that house. (43)
When Saturn enters that zodiacal sign where there is an abundance of auspicious [planets], it should be known for certain that at that time the results for the native will be auspicious. (44)
